 Crystal Palace must use rare squad depth to lift morale at Fulham 
 Go to the comments section Add to your bookmarks Share this article Crystal Palace visit Fulham in the Carabao Cup fourth round with uncommon scope to rotate. According to NY Times, Pierre Sage could name a largely changed XI after defeat at Newcastle United.
 Summer recruitment targeted Europa League depth after last season’s Conference League problems, so options are wider without leaning on the academy. Some still want youngsters to get chances, but not out of necessity.
 OneFootball Videos
 Sage needs a result, with one win in six and five of those games in the past two and a half weeks. A taxing trip to Istanbul strengthens the case for changes.
 Palace will not prioritise this competition, yet progression and a confidence boost probably outweigh adding another December fixture. Drawing on Lyon experience, Sage argues too much recovery can blunt rhythm and that some need minutes before Saturday at Tottenham, depending on profile.
 In goal, Dean Henderson is set to return from the ankle injury suffered at Craven Cottage in September. Tyrick Mitchell and Anan Khalaili could be rested for Ben Chilwell and Oscar Mingueza.
 Beyond Honest Ahanor or possibly Jefferson Lerma, centre-back options are thin, so Chris Richards, Axel Disasi and Jaydee Canvot might start. In midfield, Cheick Doucoure, who missed Middlesbrough through illness, could partner Will Hughes.
 Dario Osorio has pushed to start as the right-sided No 10 after lively cameos, with Evann Guessand another option. Yeremy Pino could feature on the opposite side and Dwight McNeil has worked his way back.
 Up front, Eddie Nketiah looks the best fit, with Jean-Philippe Mateta returning and Jorgen Strand Larsen nursing an ankle issue from Istanbul. Sage has more cover than Oliver Glasner managed, even with injuries to Strand Larsen, Quinten Timber, Chadi Riad and Takehiro Tomiyasu.
 Source: NY Times
